verdict.rationale: Missive documents its own rules engine. Rules have conditions and run actions automatically: they can create drafts, run multi-step escalations that label, notify and reassign over calendar or business-hours delays, and the pricing page lists up to 1000 rules. The evidence never lists which events trigger a rule (such as incoming message or assignment change), so the event side of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: documented catalog of trigger events and available actions, full rules documentation beyond changelog and pricing snippets, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Rules can now run in steps over time. Each step waits, checks its own conditions, then acts on the same conversation.
Escalate unanswered support emails: label at 24 hrs, notify the lead at 48, reassign at 72.
Open a rule and click “Add a step” to get started. Delays can count calendar time or business hours.
